segments.he: סיפרו לפני הר' נחמן מטולטשין ז"ל על אחד מגדולי אנ"ש שהוא עושה קידוש ביום שבת קודש בבקר על יין שרף. ולא יישר בעיניו ואמר שהוא אינו אוחז בזה ממה נפשך או אינו יוצא בקידוש או משכר את עצמו. אם הוא שותה כוס קטן אינו יוצא בקידוש כראוי ואם הוא שותה כוס גדול הלא הוא משכר את עצמו כי רבינו ז"ל אמר "בראנפין אביסעל".
segments.en: Moharan'as was once in a spiritual descent and was struggling and toiling to rise from it and illuminate himself. And meanwhile Reb Nachman of Tulchin came to him seeking spiritual sustenance. Moharan'as was agitated within: "I am struggling and toiling to illuminate myself — and now he comes and needs something from me? How can I help him?" Nonetheless Moharan'as restrained himself and said nothing to Reb Nachman. He reflected within: "Perhaps through my pressing myself to bring light to myself — through this very struggle I will make an opening to illuminate him and others as well." As is found in Rabbainu's teaching in Likutay Moharan Part II, chapter 112: "Make yourself a window for the ark" — for if one emerges from the darkness through speaking words of truth, one can do good to one who is smaller than oneself, that he too may emerge from the darkness. And so it was — light came to Moharan'as, and he illuminated Reb Nachman and future generations as well.
